description: SDLC-support products that help plan, implement, review, test, secure, modernize, or maintain software. General-purpose agent application platforms, frameworks, eval tools, and guardrails live in agents.json.

categories.description: Agents that can take tickets, prompts, issues, or tasks and independently modify repositories, run tests, and produce pull requests or deployable application changes.
Interactive coding agents embedded in IDEs, terminals, editors, or local developer environments.
Enterprise developer-platform agents that combine coding, repository intelligence, cloud context, DevSecOps workflows, governance, modernization, and organizational controls.
Agents focused on pull request review, bug finding, standards enforcement, test coverage, CI feedback, and code quality governance.

options.name: OpenAI Codex Agent
options.notes: Coding agent for CLI, desktop, IDE, and cloud tasks with skills, plugins, MCP, and repository tools. GPT-6 Sol and Luna arrived in Codex on September 22 at lower token prices than GPT-5.6, followed by GPT-6.1 Sol (September 29) and an Ultrafast mode for it on eligible plans (October 8); GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark was deprecated September 14 and GPT-5.5 retires from Codex on October 14.

options.name: Claude Code
options.notes: Coding agent spanning CLI, IDE, desktop, web, remote sessions, and team workflows, with subagents, skills, plugins, and MCP. Opus 5.5 (v2.1.280, September 22) and Sonnet 5.5 (v2.1.284, September 28) became the default models, AGENTS.md is read when no CLAUDE.md exists (September 18), and v2.1.287 (October 1) introduced Claude Mods that let plugins change deeper behaviour; Haiku 5.5 became the default Haiku in v2.1.293 (October 7).

options.name: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent
options.notes: Background coding agent for issues, pull requests, and repository tasks across GitHub and supported developer tools. The week of September 21 brought mid-conversation model switching, duplicate-issue checks, and clearer plan status for the cloud agent in Slack and Microsoft Teams; Claude Sonnet 5.5 became selectable for the coding agent on September 28.

options.name: Devin
options.notes: Autonomous software engineering agent for implementation, remediation, review, and maintenance tasks, with cloud, desktop, and customer-hosted Outpost execution. September updates add installable plugins bundling skills, rules, hooks, and MCPs (September 9), PagerDuty-triggered automations (September 11), a SWE-2 research preview in the agent selector (September 21), and a native Jira agent (September 30); October 5 adds a Terminal tab on Devin's machine.

options.name: Factory Droids
options.notes: Software development agents for CLI, desktop, web, IDE, CI/CD, and enterprise workflows. September releases add managed computers on the Pro plan (CLI 0.216.0, September 9), session forking, Databricks and ServiceNow connectors, and a /migrate command (September 26); CLI 0.237.0/Desktop 0.194.0 shipped October 9.

options.name: Replit Agent
options.notes: App-building agent that writes code, configures infrastructure, tests, and deploys projects from Replit workspaces. Since October 2, Agent users can build with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Power Mode) and GPT-6.1 Sol (Max Mode), and can have Agent wire the Jev decision model into apps through Replit AI Integrations.

options.name: Cursor Background Agents
options.notes: Asynchronous coding agents with cloud environments, branch workflows, scheduled or event-triggered subscriptions, steering, and subagents, which can also run on customer-managed machines. Cloud agents power Cursor Projects (beta, September 10), where a coordinator agent plans long-running work and delegates it to implementing agents; Rollouts (September 23) can hand detected deploy regressions to a cloud agent for a fix.

options.name: Google Antigravity 2.0
options.notes: Development environment with parallel agents, custom agents, scheduling, CLI/SDK access, and managed cloud execution. September releases add Windows sandboxing, a /plan mode that drafts plans before coding (v2.17.0, September 22), and a plugin marketplace (v2.18.1, September 28); v2.21.1 (October 7) renames Scheduled Tasks to Automations and adds advanced search, and v2.22.0 (October 8) lets plugins show UI extensions.

options.name: Mistral Vibe
options.notes: Work and coding agent with local and remote sessions, long-running tasks, skills, MCP, and file and terminal tools. September releases add /branch conversation forking, smart-approve escalation and stricter shell permission checks (v2.25.4, September 12), and readable subagent transcripts; v2.26.0 (October 6) adds /teleport to Vibe Code Web, /loop scheduling, and per-model thinking levels.

options.name: Cursor
options.notes: Agentic IDE and development workspace for coding, debugging, repository chat, and multi-agent work. Projects (beta, September 10) let a coordinator agent run months-long features or migrations on cloud agents; September 23 added Rollouts deploy monitoring and per-PR Security Review for Teams and Enterprise, and October 6 added remote control of local agents from the iOS app.

options.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
options.notes: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (renamed June 2, 2026 after Cognition's acquisition); Devin Local has replaced Cascade as the default local agent, with Cascade-specific configuration being phased out. Devin Desktop v3.7.x (Aug 2026) adds shareable Devin Local conversations, editor-file context awareness, persistent 'Always Allow' permissions, and MCP auth fixes.

options.name: Cline
options.notes: Open-source coding agent that runs in the editor, a CLI, and a desktop app, reads and writes files, executes terminal commands with user approval, supports MCP, and works with user-provided model keys. Desktop v0.0.42 (October 2) makes Connectors the default Customize tab and adds /compact; the October 7-8 releases (extension v4.1.23, CLI v3.0.70, Desktop v0.0.45) page large MCP tool output, render Mermaid diagrams inline, and move the CLI dashboard to `cline hub dashboard`.

options.name: Aider
options.notes: Terminal-first AI pair programmer with whole-repo maps, Git-native diffs and commits, support for many languages, and broad model-provider compatibility.

options.name: Continue
options.notes: Local-first IDE coding agent and assistant with model-agnostic context streaming, custom tools, and repo-aware development workflows.

options.name: Sourcegraph Cody
options.notes: AI coding assistant backed by Sourcegraph code search and codebase context. Helps understand, write, debug, and maintain code across local and remote repositories.

options.name: JetBrains Junie
options.notes: Coding agent for JetBrains IDEs and CLI that plans, edits, tests, and debugs projects. Junie Local launched August 24 with a tuned Qwen3.6-27B model running on an M5 Mac; release 26.9.22 (September 22-October 1) adds Grok 4.7, Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, and GPT-6.1 Sol, and release 26.10.5 (October 6) adds a Notification Center and mid-run steering.

options.name: Grok Build
options.notes: Local-first coding agent with planning and review modes, repository edits, shell execution, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, and subagents. xAI open-sourced Grok Build in July 2026.

options.name: Qwen Code
options.notes: Open-source coding agent for terminal, editor, desktop, and Web Shell with tools, memory, plugins, MCP, subagents, and scheduling. Desktop v0.25.0 (October 5) adds Qwen Live screen sharing into browser voice calls, in-conversation search in the Web Shell, and worktree management from the git dialog.

options.name: Kimi Code
options.notes: Moonshot AI's coding agent with terminal, web, desktop, and IDE workflows, plugins, tools, and subagents. Remote Control became generally available in v0.42 (September 9), K2.8 Preview rolled out with a 1M-token context on September 11, a Kimi Code Desktop app for macOS and Windows launched with CLI v2.0 on September 17, and CLI v2.1 (September 23) adds an experimental fullscreen mode.

options.name: GitHub Copilot
options.notes: Developer-platform assistant for completion, chat, coding-agent delegation, repository context, and code review across GitHub, IDEs, the Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app. October 1 brought dynamic multi-agent workflows and desktop-app computer use in public preview, and local sandboxing of agent tools became generally available October 7 for the CLI, Copilot app, and VS Code Agent Host sessions.

options.name: Amazon Q Developer
options.notes: AWS developer assistant for coding, review, upgrades, cloud guidance, and operations. Its IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on April 30, 2027; AWS directs developer-workflow users to Kiro, while Q in the AWS Console and chat apps continues.

options.name: Kiro
options.notes: AWS development environment (IDE, CLI, and web) for specifications, steering, hooks, powers, plugins, and governed agent workflows. Opt-in Workflows arrived in the IDE, CLI, and cloud sessions on September 30, followed by saved prompts as slash commands (CLI 2.27, October 1) and memory across chat sessions (CLI 2.29, October 9).

options.name: Gemini Code Assist Agent Mode
options.notes: Agent mode for Gemini Code Assist that uses IDE context, built-in tools, terminal actions, and MCP servers to solve multi-step software tasks. Google stopped selling new Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise subscriptions on October 9, 2026; existing subscriptions renew through 2026 and Google points users to Antigravity.

options.name: GitLab Duo with Amazon Q
options.notes: Agentic DevSecOps integration that embeds Amazon Q software development agents into GitLab workflows for feature development, quality, security, pipeline troubleshooting, and Java modernization.

options.name: CodeRabbit
options.notes: AI code review and agentic change-management platform: context-aware PR review, IDE/CLI review, Triage, Change Stack, and CodeRabbit Security. CodeRabbit Triage (September 15) ranks open PRs across repositories and gained auto-merge and auto-fix rules on September 28; CLI v0.8 (September 22) adds deep reviews and local-to-cloud Coding Agent handoff, and Security checks can block merges from October 5.

options.name: Qodo
options.notes: AI code review and governance platform with multi-agent review, repository context, Rule Miner, review effort modes, and standards governance across IDE, CLI, and Git providers. Qodo 2.10 (September 15) adds a cross-repository Software Map in beta, and Qodo 3.0 (October 1) adds PR Triage as a research preview, a review analytics dashboard, and Gerrit support.

options.name: Lovable
options.notes: App-creation agent with hosting, integrations, security scanning, and enterprise controls. September updates add Drafts for trying changes in a project copy (September 9), a Lovable API for workspace automation (September 17), and chats outside projects (September 21); October adds EU inference for Enterprise (October 1) and workspace credit limits and alerts (October 7).

options.name: Augment Code (Cosmos / Auggie)
options.notes: Coding platform combining Auggie CLI and IDE integrations with the Cosmos cloud workspace, repository context, MCP integrations, and remote agents. Cosmos added admin model controls and user groups (September 10) and Azure DevOps for all organizations, service accounts, and GitHub Enterprise Server connectors (September 17); the IDE plugins now ask for approval before reading sensitive files (September 14).

options.name: Muse Code
options.notes: Meta's terminal coding agent with background subagents, persistent session history, and planning tools. Muse Spark 1.3 with max reasoning became available September 2, and Muse Voice Transcribe powers voice dictation from September 1.

options.name: Databricks Genie Code
options.notes: Databricks assistant for code, analysis, and workspace tasks. Scheduled tasks became generally available September 1, chat branching and /btw side questions arrived September 9, and from September 25 Genie Code can build end-to-end document-processing pipelines that check extraction quality against labeled data.
